rounds.q: How many federal holidays does the US have each year?
rounds.why: Not every boss gives them: 81% of private-sector workers get paid holidays.
rounds.src: US Office of Personnel Management, Federal Holidays (2026); BLS Employee Benefits (March 2026)
rounds.fun: Eleven federal holidays a year, and 81% of private-sector workers get paid ones. Enjoy!

rounds.q: What % of US private-sector workers get paid vacation days?
rounds.why: Just 61% of state and local government workers do, partly because teachers rarely get them.
rounds.src: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employee Benefits in the United States (March 2026)
rounds.fun: Paid vacation reaches 80% of private-sector workers. Time to pick a beach!

rounds.q: How many years has the typical US worker been with their current employer?
rounds.why: The exact midpoint is 4.1 years, but for workers ages 55 to 64 it is 9.6 years.
rounds.src: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employee Tenure (January 2026)
rounds.fun: About 4 years in and counting. Workers ages 55 to 64 have stuck around for 9.6!

rounds.q: On days they work, what % of US workers do some or all of it at home?
rounds.why: Women (38%) are more likely to work at home than men (31%).
rounds.src: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey (2025 data)
rounds.fun: On a work day, 35% clock in from home at least a little. Slippers count as work shoes!

rounds.q: On an average weekend day, what % of employed Americans do some work?
rounds.why: On an average weekday, 81% of employed people work.
rounds.src: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey (2025 data)
rounds.fun: Weekends are not all rest. 30% of workers put in some work, next to 81% on a weekday.
